Don’t get me wrong, this is a well put together and beautiful app to use. I love the experience of using it but this could have been my go to note taking app if they would just implement a folder system instead of hashtags. I truly hope one day they can add this as a feature.

That being said there’s not much else to dislike about this app. The search is powerful, the organization is simple but capable, it’s very nice to look at, it has a focus on privacy, the import and export (especially) are amazing, it honestly never overwhelms me and never gets in my way but also is there with everything i need like tags, exports, callback urls, shortcuts app, etc. 

I would prefer icloud drive MD files over cloudkit but I definitely prefer icloud anything over some half baked AWS instance that you often find on other note apps. Also frankly the very good export system almost makes having the icloud drive files unnecessary anyway

Overall, despite my occasional minor grievances with some missing features bear is easily the best notes app I’ve come across and I am happy to open it and use it every day

title.label: This is the best notes app

Bear is one of those rare gems that you come across once in a great while.

- Simple: It has a simple interface, which allows you to focus on writing. It uses Markdown (which I was not a fan of at first), but now I’m a convert and prefer writing in Markdown if possible!

- Powerful: The killer feature of Bear is its tagging system combined with the [[Wikilinks]] feature. There is no folder structure which I’ve read some complain about. However, Bear uses nested tags (think: #folder/sub-folder/sub-sub-folder) and I find placing this inline in my note is truly a great way to organize notes.

- Beautiful: I actually want to do all my writing in Bear. That about sums it up!

- Secure: Bear doesn’t get access to your files. It syncs through iCloud as encrypted files, so Apple can’t access them either. This is the best of all worlds when it comes to sync AND security.

As of writing (Feb 2021) there has been a lack of feature updates, but this is understandable since they are rewriting the app from the ground up to accommodate the increasing demand for new features. Sometimes, you have to rebuild from the ground up and while it is NOT FAST, it is the RIGHT call. Meanwhile, they have kept the current app usable and updated. Well done Bear!

P.S. - Bear’s only real competition is Obsidian (free local app), which is powerful, but not necessarily simple. I’ve tried Roam Research (paid web app), but it actually has way to much functionality (yes this is possible) and is to expensive ($165/year which would pay for Bear Pro for 11 years... my vote is Bear).

title.label: By far my favorite note-taking app

content.label:
I have an iPad pro and frequently use the Apple Pencil and have been using GoodNotes/Notability for handwritten notes and Bear for text-based notes.  I have no idea how I missed it, but I never knew Bear had sketching/drawing capabilities built into it.  And now, I’ll probably never touch Notability again (maybe).

Bear is super solid and responsive.  The developers are amazing and interact frequently on the Bear-dedicated subreddit over on reddit.com.  They are always a pleasure to deal with, and they take user feedback seriously.  It feels great to be heard when you ask for a feature enhancement/new feature on an already-amazing app.  Tagging, search, and sync work so well.  Nesting tags in folders is so intuitive and simple that organization can be super simple or fairly complex, however you want it to be.  The interface is super pleasant and simple; it reminds me of WriteRoom, one of my favorite Mac word process apps.  There’s very little on the screen to distract you.  The export options are also great.  I tend to send everything out to PDF just to have archives I can save somewhere outside the app, and that ability is essential to me.  I’ve had notes get erased from other apps, in spite of online backups/syncing within those apps.  The ability to export and manage my own archive in addition to the one in the app is really reassuring.

I can’t recommend this app enough.  I pay for Pro, and it’s worth far more than what it costs.  I frequently go through my subscriptions and re-evaluate what I really need.  This app is never up for reconsideration; this subscription never really gets questioned.  I really, really love this app.

title.label: Exactly What I Was Looking For

content.label:
I was a longtime Evernote user until I felt alienated by their recent v10 update, which (to my dismay) immediately left me researching alternatives.

I test-drove several other popular note-taking apps, looking for something simple yet functional. Nothing felt great, but as soon as I found Bear, I instantly fell in love.

- The import to Evernote was seamless, and the formatting of my notes was mostly preserved.
- The UI is absolutely gorgeous, and using the app is silky smooth, even with 500+ notes. It just feels like a finely-tuned native app all the time.
- The tagging system is flexible enough to allow for multiple levels of hierarchy, so if you need to organize your notes into nested folders, you can do so. The tags are a little weird to set up at first, but once you do, management is fairly simple and transparent.
- Note formatting is in the Markdown syntax, which I actually enjoy as a programmer, but it may be a little weird for those used to pure rich-text editing. But Bear helps bridge this gap because it supports all the same keyboard shortcuts, lists are automatically continued when you Enter down, etc.—it still feels pretty natural.
- There are little graphics of bears here and there (like a bear holding an hourglass when you import), which you can't help but smile at, giving you the sense that the app is created by people who care and have fun.
- Their support portal is quite helpful, and their social media feeds are updated regularly with new tricks that enhance your workflow. They also seem very conscious of their community, and are receptive to user feedback.
- The subscription cost is less than half the price of an Evernote subscription, yet I'm getting so much more bang for my buck.

Markdown as a standard is a widely used syntax that Bear slightly expands upon with their use of tags so as to support inter-linking what you write. Supporting whitespace by wrapping text between #two hashtags# is a welcome innovative idea. But the welcome changes end there.

Bear locks down images into iCloud storage but in such a way that you cannot actually access them. Bear also provides weak image manipulation tools which do not include cropping. This extends into the drawing tool, where canvas size is automatically chosen by wherever a stroke may have landed. In other words, you could draw a lovely image but it could be uselessly and awkwardly bordered by whitespace, often shoved in a corner. I think they expect users to use the whole canvas every time which is stupid to assume.

Then there are the export options that are still severely lacking. Many static site generators rely on markdown and are thirsty for an application like Bear so that simple blogs can be maintained. Git integration is not an option. Again, flat file storage for images is not an option. Even on Desktop, you are locked in to only working on iCloud which means you can’t get to work on a regular folder of text files. That’s pretty lame in my opinion!

I want to like Bear, but it always feels broken in these ways.

I have close to 1000 notes with hundreds of attachments and performance remains good. Looking forward to better pencil support, web app and tables and I know all of these are in development.  Doesn’t have note sharing or version history, both of which would be good to have someday.
